mutants.title: STARTED tally counts only nPeriod-1 blocks, dropping the first block of the period
mutants.description:
> This description is AI generated, mistakes can be made.

**Intent:** Break the BIP 9 rule that the signalling tally covers the whole retarget period: the oldest block of the window (the first block of the period) is never examined, so a deployment needs `threshold` signals out of `period - 1` blocks. The case for calling this critical rather than high is that it is a pure consensus divergence with no attacker needed; the case for a lower label is that it only bites when the period is within one block of the threshold.

**Behaviour change:** Original tallies blocks [first..last] of the period (nPeriod blocks). Mutant tallies [first+1..last] (nPeriod-1 blocks). Whenever the first block of the period signals and the remaining blocks give exactly threshold-1 ... threshold signals, the two disagree on whether the period reaches threshold, i.e. on LOCKED_IN vs STARTED/FAILED.

**Trigger:** A mainnet deployment period in which exactly `threshold` (1916) of the 2016 blocks signal and one of the signalling blocks is the first block of the period: unpatched nodes go LOCKED_IN and, one period later, ACTIVE and start enforcing the new rules; a mutated node stays STARTED. Reproducible in regtest with -vbparams testdummy:<start>:<end> and a 144-block period containing exactly 108 signals including block 0 of the period.

**Spec violation:** BIP 9: 'we tally the bits set ... int count = 0; walk = block; for (i = 0; i < 2016; i++) { walk = walk.parent; if (...) count++; } if (count >= threshold) return LOCKED_IN;' - the tally is over the full 2016-block retarget period.

**Severity if undetected:** critical

**Why tests miss it:** walked all six chains of versionbits_tests.cpp:versionbits_test by hand (the marginal period at Mine(3000,...) has a non-signalling block 2000 in both the FAILED and the exact-900 LOCKED_IN scenario, so the count is unchanged); both chains of check_computeblockversion (firstChain never signals; secondChain signals every block, 143 >= 108); rpc_blockchain.py's 144-block all-signalling period at height 287 (143 >= 108); grepped src/test and test/functional for other callers of GetStateFor

**Plausibility:** Off-by-one in a hand-written walk-back loop is the single most common mistake in this kind of code, and `i = 1` reads like a deliberate 'the first step is the block itself' adjustment - especially since BIP 9's own pseudocode advances `walk = walk.parent` before testing, which invites exactly this confusion.

**Equivalence risk:** It is a no-op for any period where the first block's signal is not decisive - which is almost every period in practice, including every period in the existing tests. It changes an observable state only when the tally sits exactly on the threshold boundary.
mutants.notes: mutant-harness operator: boundary; location: AbstractThresholdConditionChecker::GetStateFor (STARTED case) lines 87-92

mutants.title: BIP9Stats.possible uses a strict > so a period that can still exactly reach threshold is reported impossible
mutants.description:
> This description is AI generated, mistakes can be made.

**Intent:** Break the documented meaning of BIP9Stats::possible ('False if there are not enough blocks left in this period to pass activation threshold') at its boundary: the case where every single remaining block must signal is still possible, but is now reported as hopeless.

**Behaviour change:** With period 2016 / threshold 1916, after exactly 100 non-signalling blocks the original still reports possible=true (the fork activates if every remaining block signals); the mutant reports possible=false and getdeploymentinfo then omits both 'threshold' and 'possible' from the statistics object only when threshold is also 0 - in the STARTED case it reports "possible": false while activation is still achievable.

**Trigger:** getdeploymentinfo (or the REST /deploymentinfo endpoint) on any node whose current period has exactly period-threshold non-signalling blocks so far - e.g. regtest testdummy with 36 of the first 36 blocks of a 144-block period not signalling, then querying at any point before the period ends.

**Spec violation:** versionbits.h: '/** False if there are not enough blocks left in this period to pass activation threshold */ bool possible' - with elapsed-count == period-threshold there are exactly enough blocks left.

**Severity if undetected:** low

**Why tests miss it:** grepped 'possible' across test/functional (only rpc_blockchain.py, where count == elapsed so both sides are true) and src/test (only the fuzz target); GetStateStatisticsFor is never called from versionbits_tests.cpp

**Plausibility:** The expression is already written in a slightly awkward 'slack >= deficit' form; flipping it to a strict inequality is the classic off-by-one a reader cannot check without re-deriving the algebra, and no reviewer sees a failing test.

**Equivalence risk:** Only differs on the exact boundary (elapsed-count == period-threshold); every test period so far has elapsed == count, where both forms are true.

mutants.title: signalling_blocks is filled newest-first, reversing the getdeploymentinfo signalling string
mutants.description:
> This description is AI generated, mistakes can be made.

**Intent:** Break the chronological ordering of the per-block signalling vector that rpc/blockchain.cpp renders as the 'signalling' string of '#' and '-' characters; the walk is backwards, so indexing by elapsed instead of by the remaining-block counter reverses it.

**Behaviour change:** For a period whose blocks signalled in the pattern '##--#' the original returns '##--#' and the mutant returns '#--##'. Identical whenever all (or no) blocks in the period signal. Vector bounds are unaffected (elapsed-1 runs 0..size-1), so there is no exception, just wrong data.

**Trigger:** getdeploymentinfo on a chain where signalling is mixed within the current period - e.g. regtest testdummy after mining 3 signalling blocks and then 2 blocks with -blockversion set to a non-signalling value: the 'signalling' field reads '--###' instead of '###--'.

**Spec violation:** rpc/blockchain.cpp documents the field as the per-block signalling record of the period in block order ('identifies blocks that signalled with # and blocks that did not with -'), which consumers index by position within the period.

**Severity if undetected:** low

**Why tests miss it:** grepped 'signalling' in test/functional (only rpc_blockchain.py, whose period is 100% signalling so the string is all '#' either way) and in src/test (only the fuzz target)

**Plausibility:** `elapsed - 1` looks like the obvious index of 'the block we just examined', and the alternative (`blocks_in_period` after its decrement) is genuinely obscure; a reviewer has to notice that the loop walks backwards to see the difference.

**Equivalence risk:** Invisible unless the period contains both signalling and non-signalling blocks, and invisible to any consumer that only counts '#' characters.

mutants.title: getdeploymentinfo keeps reporting threshold/possible while a deployment is LOCKED_IN
mutants.description:
> This description is AI generated, mistakes can be made.

**Intent:** Remove the deliberate suppression of threshold/possible once a deployment has locked in. rpc/blockchain.cpp only emits those two fields when `threshold > 0 || possible`, so zeroing them is how the RPC signals 'the threshold no longer applies'.

**Behaviour change:** While current_state == LOCKED_IN the original emits statistics with only period/elapsed/count; the mutant additionally emits "threshold": 108 and "possible": <whatever this period's signalling happens to give>, i.e. it tells the operator the fork can still fail to reach threshold when it is already irreversibly locked in.

**Trigger:** getdeploymentinfo on regtest at any height in [288, 431] (testdummy is LOCKED_IN there, with min_activation_height unreached only if configured; with default params it is LOCKED_IN for exactly one period): the bip9.statistics object gains threshold/possible, and possible reads false as soon as more than period-threshold blocks of the new period fail to signal.

**Spec violation:** Contradicts the RPC's own contract in rpc/blockchain.cpp (threshold/possible are only meaningful while signalling can still change the outcome) and BIP 9's LOCKED_IN semantics: once locked in, the transition to ACTIVE is unconditional.

**Severity if undetected:** low

**Why tests miss it:** rpc_blockchain.py:_test_getdeploymentinfo only samples heights 207 and 287, where current_state is 'started' and this branch is not taken on master either; grepped test/functional for 'locked_in' (one hit, that same status_next assertion) and src/test for VersionBitsCache::Info (no unit test exists); the fuzz target never calls Info

**Plausibility:** It reads like the removal of a redundant special case - the numbers it deletes are the same ones the statistics struct already carries - and the surrounding `has_signal` guard still mentions LOCKED_IN, so nothing looks obviously missing.

**Equivalence risk:** Nothing changes unless a caller inspects statistics while current_state is exactly LOCKED_IN, which is a one-period window per deployment.

mutants.title: active_since is overwritten with tip+1 for already-active deployments
mutants.description:
> This description is AI generated, mistakes can be made.

**Intent:** Break the reported activation height: ACTIVE is a terminal state, so whenever current_state is ACTIVE next_state is ACTIVE too, and un-chaining the branches makes the second assignment always win.

**Behaviour change:** For an active bip9 deployment the original reports the height at which it activated (BIP9Info::active_since = since); the mutant reports the height of the next block, so getdeploymentinfo's bip9 'height' field tracks the tip and changes with every block. The 'active' boolean is unaffected (active_since <= nHeight+1 still holds).

**Trigger:** getdeploymentinfo on regtest once testdummy is ACTIVE (height >= ~432 with default regtest params): 'height' reads <tip+1> on every call instead of the fixed activation height; on mainnet the same would apply to any activated bip9 softfork.

**Spec violation:** versionbits.h: '/** Height at which the deployment is active, if known. May be in the future. */ std::optional<int> active_since' - and rpc/blockchain.cpp exposes it as the deployment's activation height, the bip9 counterpart of a buried deployment's fixed 'height'.

**Severity if undetected:** medium

**Why tests miss it:** rpc_blockchain.py never reaches an ACTIVE testdummy (it stops at height 287 and asserts 'active': False); grepped test/functional for softfork_active/getdeploymentinfo users - all of them (feature_cltv, feature_dersig, wallet_signrawtransactionwithwallet, feature_bip68_sequence, feature_csv_activation) query buried deployments, which take the other SoftForkDescPushBack overload; interface_rest.py only compares REST against the same RPC

**Plausibility:** Splitting an if/else-if into two ifs is a routine-looking edit (e.g. while adding a third case), and both branches assign the same field, so the diff reads as a no-op unless you remember that ACTIVE is terminal.

**Equivalence risk:** For a deployment that is not ACTIVE the behaviour is identical; the divergence needs current_state == ACTIVE, which no test ever inspects.
mutants.notes: mutant-harness operator: scope; location: VersionBitsCache::Info lines 219-223

mutants.title: getblocktemplate files ACTIVE deployments under locked_in instead of active
mutants.description:
> This description is AI generated, mistakes can be made.

**Intent:** Drop activated softforks out of getblocktemplate's 'rules' list and, with them, the guard in rpc/mining.cpp that refuses to serve a template to a client which has not declared support for a non-optional active rule; the template also starts signalling a bit for an already-active deployment.

**Behaviour change:** Original: an ACTIVE deployment appears in the template's 'rules' array and a client that did not list a non-optional rule gets 'Support for <rule> rule requires explicit client support'. Mutant: it appears in 'vbavailable' instead, rpc/mining.cpp ORs its mask into the template's nVersion (so blocks keep signalling after activation, contrary to ComputeBlockVersion), and the client-support check never fires.

**Trigger:** getblocktemplate on a regtest node past testdummy activation (height >= ~432): 'rules' loses 'testdummy', 'vbavailable' gains it, and the returned 'version' has bit 28 set again. On mainnet the same would happen to any future softfork after activation, including one whose gbt_optional_rule is false.

**Spec violation:** BIP 9 on signalling: 'Miners should continue setting the bit in LOCKED_IN phase so uptake is visible' - signalling is supposed to stop at ACTIVE, which is why ComputeBlockVersion only sets the bit for STARTED/LOCKED_IN. Also breaks getblocktemplate's documented 'rules' contract (BIP 9 / BIP 22 'rules: specific block rules that are to be enforced').

**Severity if undetected:** medium

**Why tests miss it:** grepped test/functional for vbavailable/vbrequired (no hits at all) and for 'rules' (feature_segwit.py checks the hardcoded '!segwit' entry; mining_basic.py:489 asserts the exact list ['csv','!segwit','taproot'], which passes on master only because testdummy is not ACTIVE at that height, and mutation only ever removes entries there); mining_basic.py's template 'version' assertion is made at height 200, where testdummy is STARTED

**Plausibility:** Three consecutive cases each doing try_emplace into a differently-named member is exactly the shape that produces a copy-paste slip, and neither map is read by any test.

**Equivalence risk:** Identical output until some bip9 deployment reaches ACTIVE; for optional rules (testdummy) the only differences are which JSON object the name lands in and a set bit in the template version.

mutants.title: Unknown-softfork warning uses the mainnet 90% threshold on testnet and signet
mutants.description:
> This description is AI generated, mistakes can be made.

**Intent:** Narrow the 'this is a test network' predicate from 'any chain but mainnet' to 'regtest only', so testnet3, testnet4 and signet fall back to the hardcoded mainnet constants for the warning checker.

**Behaviour change:** On testnet/testnet4/signet the original requires 1512 of 2016 blocks (75%) signalling an unknown bit before warning; the mutant requires 1815 (90%). (period is 2016 on those chains either way, so only the threshold moves.) A real unknown-softfork activation on testnet at 75-89% support now produces no warning at all, while the node still follows the chain.

**Trigger:** A signet or testnet4 node, out of IBD, receiving a retarget period in which ~80% of blocks set an unknown bit in 0..4: master warns 'Unknown new rules activated (versionbit N)' and fires -alertnotify, the mutant stays silent.

**Spec violation:** BIP 9 selection guidelines / Core convention: test networks use the 75% threshold ('1512 for testchains'), which is precisely what the comment on the next line still claims the code does.

**Severity if undetected:** low

**Why tests miss it:** feature_versionbits_warning.py is the only test of this class and runs on regtest, where IsMockableChain() is also true (kernel/chainparams.cpp: m_is_mockable_chain is set true only for regtest), so it is unaffected; no functional test runs the warning path on testnet/signet; versionbits_tests.cpp never instantiates WarningBitsConditionChecker (it is in an anonymous namespace)

**Plausibility:** IsTestChain() and IsMockableChain() are adjacent one-line accessors in kernel/chainparams.h and are routinely confused; picking the 'more specific' one looks like a tightening rather than a bug.

**Equivalence risk:** On mainnet and regtest the two predicates select the same branch, so only testnet/signet behave differently - and there the difference is one threshold value that no test exercises.

mutants.title: Warning checker drops the MinBIP9WarningHeight guard, re-warning about historical activations
mutants.description:
> This description is AI generated, mistakes can be made.

**Intent:** Remove the guard whose entire purpose is to stop the node from re-discovering the CSV, segwit and taproot activations as 'unknown' softforks.

**Behaviour change:** On mainnet the warning state machine now tallies the 2016-era CSV (bit 0), segwit (bit 1) and 2021 taproot (bit 2) signalling periods, all of which exceeded 90%, so those bits reach the terminal ACTIVE state. Every mainnet node past IBD then reports 'Unknown new rules activated (versionbit 0/1/2)' in getnetworkinfo/getmininginfo and fires -alertnotify, permanently and for every new tip.

**Trigger:** Any mainnet (or testnet3) node that finishes IBD and connects a block: validation.cpp:2912 calls CheckUnknownActivations, which now returns bits 0, 1 and 2 as active.

**Spec violation:** consensus/params.h: '/** Don't warn about unknown BIP 9 activations below this height. This prevents us from warning about the CSV, segwit and taproot activations. */ int MinBIP9WarningHeight'.

**Severity if undetected:** medium

**Why tests miss it:** MinBIP9WarningHeight is 0 on regtest, signet and testnet4 (kernel/chainparams.cpp lines 361/518/598), so the clause is vacuously true in every functional test, including feature_versionbits_warning.py; only mainnet (711648) and testnet3 (2013984) set it, and no test runs the warning path there; grepped src/test for MinBIP9WarningHeight - no hits

**Plausibility:** It is one clause of a four-clause boolean; a contributor cleaning up Condition() (or moving the height check to the caller) could easily drop it, and no regtest-based test will ever complain.

**Equivalence risk:** Behaviourally identical on every chain whose MinBIP9WarningHeight is 0 - which is every chain the test suite runs.

mutants.title: Warning checker counts blocks whose top 3 version bits are not 001
mutants.description:
> This description is AI generated, mistakes can be made.

**Intent:** Break BIP 9's rule that a block whose top bits are not 001 signals nothing, for the warning checker only (VersionBitsConditionChecker::Condition keeps it), so legacy or non-versionbits block versions are counted as signalling unknown softforks.

**Behaviour change:** Blocks with nVersion outside [0x20000000, 0x3FFFFFFF] now contribute to the tally: e.g. version 4 blocks set bit 2, version 2 blocks set bit 1, version 1 blocks set bit 0, and any BIP 8-style 0x40000000-family version counts for whichever low bit it happens to set. A period dominated by such blocks drives the warning state machine to LOCKED_IN/ACTIVE and raises 'Unknown new rules activated (versionbit N)' on a chain where nobody signalled anything.

**Trigger:** A chain where >=90% (mainnet) / 75% (test chains) of a retarget period carries a legacy version - e.g. a regtest/signet chain built by a test harness that mines version-4 blocks, or a mainnet miner deliberately mining old-style versions - makes the node warn its operator that unknown rules activated.

**Spec violation:** BIP 9: 'When a block nVersion does not have top bits 001, it is treated as if all bits are 0 for the purposes of deployments.'

**Severity if undetected:** low

**Why tests miss it:** feature_versionbits_warning.py mines only VB_TOP_BITS-based versions (0x20000008 / 0x20000020) plus node-generated 0x20000000 blocks, so no period reaches the threshold on any low bit (the genesis block's version 1 is 1 block out of 144); no functional test asserts that node warnings are empty (grepped 'warnings' across test/functional - all hits are wallet/descriptor warnings); versionbits_tests.cpp never builds a WarningBitsConditionChecker

**Plausibility:** The remaining bit test looks self-sufficient, and the top-mask clause is easy to read as redundant with the identical check already done in VersionBitsConditionChecker::Condition; the diff is a single deleted line in a boolean chain.

**Equivalence risk:** In practice essentially all modern blocks carry top bits 001, so on today's mainnet the tally is unchanged; the mutant only bites on legacy or exotic version numbers.
mutants.notes: mutant-harness operator: condition; location: WarningBitsConditionChecker::Condition lines 326

mutants.title: CheckUnknownActivations never scans the top BIP 323 signalling bit
mutants.description:
> This description is AI generated, mistakes can be made.

**Intent:** Shorten the warning scan to bits 0..3, leaving bit 4 - a perfectly valid BIP 323 signalling bit - completely unmonitored.

**Behaviour change:** An unknown softfork deployed on bit 4 locks in and activates without the node ever emitting 'Unknown new rules activated (versionbit 4)', so the operator gets no indication that the network may be enforcing rules this node does not know. Bits 0..3 behave as before.

**Trigger:** A mainnet (or regtest) chain in which >=90% (75% on test chains) of a retarget period sets bit 4 and no known deployment uses it: master warns and fires -alertnotify, the mutant is silent forever.

**Spec violation:** BIP 323: bits 5..28 'are reserved for nonce use and removed from BIP8 and BIP9 specifications ... bits 5-28 inclusive will be ignored for soft-fork signalling and unknown soft-fork warnings' - i.e. bits 0..4 inclusive must still be watched, which is exactly what VERSIONBITS_NUM_BITS == 5 encodes.

**Severity if undetected:** medium

**Why tests miss it:** feature_versionbits_warning.py is the only test of this function and uses VB_UNKNOWN_BIT = 3 (its VB_IGNORED_BIT = 5 is already outside the loop on master); grepped src/test for CheckUnknownActivations and m_warning_caches - no unit test or fuzz target covers them

**Plausibility:** 'NUM_BITS - 1' reads like an author who thinks of the constant as the highest usable bit index, and the loop still visibly covers 'the versionbits range', so a reviewer scanning for the usual `<=` mistake sees nothing alarming.

**Equivalence risk:** No difference at all unless something actually signals on bit 4; every other bit is still scanned, so the warning system looks fully functional in testing.
mutants.notes: mutant-harness operator: boundary; location: VersionBitsCache::CheckUnknownActivations lines 337

mutants.title: No advance warning while an unknown softfork is merely LOCKED_IN
mutants.description:
> This description is AI generated, mistakes can be made.

**Intent:** Drop the half of this function's documented contract that reports deployments which are locked in but not yet active, removing the one retarget period (~2 weeks on mainnet) of advance notice an operator gets before unknown rules start being enforced.

**Behaviour change:** Original returns (bit, false) while the unknown deployment is LOCKED_IN, and validation.cpp logs 'Unknown new rules activated (versionbit N)' with each new tip as a pre-activation warning; the mutant returns nothing until the deployment is already ACTIVE, at which point the operator is told only after the fact.

**Trigger:** Any chain where an unknown bit passes the signalling threshold: during the following retarget period master emits the warning in the UpdateTip log line, the mutant emits nothing.

**Spec violation:** versionbits.h: 'Returns a vector containing the bit number used for signalling and a bool indicating the deployment is likely to be ACTIVE, rather than merely LOCKED_IN' - the bool exists precisely because LOCKED_IN is reported too.

**Severity if undetected:** low

**Why tests miss it:** feature_versionbits_warning.py only asserts the persistent warning (kernel::Warning::UNKNOWN_NEW_RULES_ACTIVATED, i.e. the ACTIVE branch) via getmininginfo/getnetworkinfo and the alertnotify file; the LOCKED_IN branch only reaches warning_messages -> UpdateTipLog, and no test greps debug.log for it; no unit test calls CheckUnknownActivations

**Plausibility:** The leftover `state == ACTIVE` argument in the emplace_back looks like a tidy-up artifact rather than a symptom, and 'only warn about what actually activated' is an argument a reviewer might accept on its face.

**Equivalence risk:** The ACTIVE warning still fires one period later, so on any chain observed over time the operator eventually sees the same message - only the early notice is lost.
mutants.notes: mutant-harness operator: condition; location: VersionBitsCache::CheckUnknownActivations lines 340

mutants.mutatedCode: const bool has_signal = (STARTED == next_state || LOCKED_IN == next_state);
mutants.title: BIP9 statistics are selected by the next block's state instead of the current one
mutants.description:
> This description is AI generated, mistakes can be made.

**Intent:** Swap the state that decides whether signalling information is applicable, so getdeploymentinfo reports (or hides) the statistics block for the wrong period at every state boundary.

**Behaviour change:** At the last block of a period where the state changes, the two disagree: with current_state == STARTED and next_state == FAILED or ACTIVE the mutant omits 'bit', 'statistics' and 'signalling' entirely from the RPC output for a period that did signal; with current_state == DEFINED and next_state == STARTED it emits them for a period in which signalling had no meaning yet.

**Trigger:** getdeploymentinfo at the last block of the period in which a deployment times out (STARTED -> FAILED) or activates (LOCKED_IN -> ACTIVE) - e.g. regtest testdummy at height 431 with default params: master reports the statistics/signalling of the just-finished period, the mutant reports none.

**Spec violation:** rpc/blockchain.cpp treats the statistics object as describing the period the queried block belongs to (its 'status', not its 'status_next'); BIP9Info documents stats as 'For states where signalling is applicable', i.e. the current state.

**Severity if undetected:** low

**Why tests miss it:** rpc_blockchain.py samples height 207 (started/started) and 287 (started/locked_in); has_signal is true under both readings at both heights, so the expected JSON is unchanged; no unit test or fuzz target calls VersionBitsCache::Info

**Plausibility:** current_state and next_state are computed two lines apart and used two lines later; picking the wrong one is a one-word slip, and the following line still reads `if (LOCKED_IN == current_state)` so the function looks internally consistent.

**Equivalence risk:** current_state and next_state are equal for all but the last block of a transitioning period, so the two versions agree on the overwhelming majority of queries.
mutants.notes: mutant-harness operator: state; location: VersionBitsCache::Info lines 210
